item.title: Taketa & Oka Castle Ruins — Guide
item.description: The ruins of Oka Castle (Oka-jō), above the town of Taketa in inland Oita, are among the most spectacular and atmospheric castle ruins in Japan. Built on a natural rock plateau high on a steep ridge, this formidable mountaintop fortress once controlled the region, but its buildings were demolished in the Meiji era, leaving only the vast, sweeping stone walls and ramparts perched dramatically along the clifftops. Walking the ruins today, with panoramic views over the surrounding mountains and the Kuju range — especially stunning wreathed in autumn colours or a sea of clouds — is a moving experience.
